data.name: Mushtaaq
data.gender_notes: Mushtaaq is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root sh-t-q, meaning to long for, to desire, and to yearn. In Islamic context, Mushtaaq signifies one who is longing for Allah's love and Paradise. The name Mushtaaq carries the meaning “Longing, Desiring” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mushtaaq usually hope their child will grow to embody longing, desiring and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the deep longing and yearning for Allah's love and Paradise.
data.etymology: Mushtaaq belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Longing, Desiring.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mushtaaq total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidāyah wa l-Nihāyah, vol. VIII, p. 175 The name Mushtaaq carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mushtaaq ibn 'Amr al-Khuza'i was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). He was the ruler of Kufa when Imam 'Ali (ra) was away. Mushtaaq was killed by a group of rebels who were dissatisfied with 'Ali's rule during the First Fitna.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Tabari's Tarikh al-Rusul wa l- Muluk, vol. III, p. 398 The name Mushtaaq carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mushtaaq ibn 'Amr al-Khuza'i was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). After the death of the Prophet, Mushtaaq supported 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (ra), the first caliph, against 'Umar ibn Al-Khattab's claim to the caliphate. During the Battle of the Camel, Mushtaaq commanded the right wing of 'Ali's army.
